name: Homity Pie
steps: Rub the cold butter into the flour until it resembles coarse crumbs. Add 3 g salt, then cold water a spoonful at a time, pressing just until the pastry holds together; do not knead it. Flatten into a disc, wrap and chill for 20 minutes so the butter stays cold.

Peel and cut the potatoes into 2-cm cubes. Bring the measured 1800 ml water to a boil with 5 g salt and cook the potatoes for 12–15 minutes until just tender, not falling apart. Drain thoroughly and let steam-dry. Thinly slice the onions and mince the garlic.

Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the onions for 10–12 minutes until soft and lightly golden; add the garlic for the final minute. Mix with the potatoes, cream, chopped parsley, black pepper, half the grated vegetarian cheddar and the remaining 2 g salt. Fold gently to keep some potato chunks intact.

Heat the oven to 200°C. Roll the chilled pastry to about 3 mm thick and line a 23-cm tart tin, leaving an open top. Prick the base, line with baking paper and fill with baking beans or dry rice. Blind-bake for 15 minutes, remove paper and weights, then bake 5 more minutes until the base looks dry.

Spoon the potato mixture into the pastry shell and scatter the remaining cheddar over the top. Bake at 200°C for 25–30 minutes until the crust is golden, the filling is hot all the way through and the cheese has browned in spots. If the edge colours too quickly, shield it with a strip of foil.
Rest the pie for 10 minutes before cutting into four generous wedges. Serve warm; a slice should hold its shape and show distinct pieces of potato and onion inside the crisp open pastry shell.
tips: Use vegetarian cheddar made without animal rennet. Thoroughly drying the boiled potatoes and blind-baking the pastry keeps the bottom crisp. This is an open pie; do not cover the filling with a pastry lid.
passiveTime: 20 minutes pastry chilling and 10 minutes pie resting
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
